subject: Control-plane segregation and egress policy brief for regulated Dedicated/Private deployments

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As part of our SIG procurement review, the security and procurement teams are asking for a concise artifact (1-2 page narrative + diagrams) that explains how Redwood separates the control plane from the data plane for Dedicated and Private deployments, and what egress/egress-filtering controls are applied. Specifically they want:

- A short diagram showing control-plane boundaries for Dedicated (Redwood-managed control plane) vs Private (customer-controlled control plane).
- A table of egress destinations/ports that the control plane needs to talk to (for patching, telemetry, licensing) and whether those can be restricted to fixed IP ranges.
- Confirmation on whether data plane traffic (model inference payloads / KV caches) ever transits Redwood-managed networks for Private deployments.

Our deadline to close the SIG evidence pack is Aug 24. Can you share a short brief and any diagram/CSV with the egress matrix? If you prefer, a 30-minute walk-through with our security team would also work.

Thanks,

Hi team — attaching the first-pass package. Summary below, full details in attached files (control_plane_boundary_summary.pdf, segregation_map_v2.svg, egress_policy_matrix.xlsx).

Executive summary (2 paragraphs) —
- Architecture: Redwood Dedicated uses a Redwood-managed control plane that orchestrates Dedicated GPU pools; the control plane is logically isolated from customer data plane and runs in a separate VPC per region. For Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem options), customers may choose a customer-managed control plane (private control plane) or Redwood-managed control plane with private network peering. In both models, inference traffic (model inputs/outputs and KV cache state) is segregated from control-plane telemetry.

- Controls: Control plane components communicate to external services for patching, telemetry, and license checks over tightly scoped egress rules. We provide static IP ranges for control-plane egress for customers that require IP allowlisting; these are published and can be scoped to region and environment (prod/staging). For Private with customer-managed control plane, egress is subject to the customer's network policy and may be routed over private interconnects (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute).

Technical highlights (short):
- Logical separation: control-plane microservices (orchestration, autoscaler, fleet manager) run in separate subnets and are tagged as control-plane; data-plane inference nodes are in separate subnets with strict security group policies (no inbound from control-plane except orchestrated orchestration ports).
- Mutual TLS + mTLS auth: all service-to-service control-plane traffic uses mTLS with short-lived certs issued by Redwood's internal CA; customer-facing data-plane endpoints use mutually authenticated TLS where required.
- KV cache and prefix caching: KV caches are pinned to data-plane nodes and are never forwarded to Redwood-managed telemetry systems for Private on-prem deployments. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed), telemetry collects lightweight metrics but not model payloads.
- Egress details: egress_policy_matrix.xlsx lists: destination FQDNs/IP ranges, required ports (TCP 443, 123 for NTP where applicable), frequency, and whether static IP allocation is available. We can offer static egress IPs for the control plane in the dedicated offering and for Redwood-managed private control planes via NAT gateway pools.

Requested deliverables included in attachments:
- control_plane_boundary_summary.pdf (one-page narrative + short Q&A)
- segregation_map_v2.svg (diagram showing control vs data plane boundaries for Dedicated, Private-managed-control-plane, and Private-customer-control-plane variants)
- egress_policy_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet with destinations, ports, static-ip-availability, and justification)

Notes / caveats:
- For air-gapped on-prem installations, we support an offline package and customer-driven patching; that option requires a different evidence set which I note in the PDF.
- SOC 2: these separation and egress controls map to CC6 and CC7 controls; we can provide the mapping table on request.

If Anne/procurement want IP ranges in CIDR form in the spreadsheet, we can export them as plain CSV on request.

-Karthik

Hi Karthik —

Thank you, this looks useful. Quick clarifying questions from our security reviewer:
1) For the Redwood-managed control plane in Dedicated, does control-plane egress always originate from a published set of static IPs per region, or are there cases where ephemeral NAT IPs would be used?
2) For Private deployments where the customer elects a Redwood-managed control plane with private peering, can telemetry/updates be configured to route only over the private interconnect (i.e., never go over public internet)?
3) The segregation map shows KV caches pinned to data-plane nodes for Private on-prem. Can you confirm that those caches are not backed up to Redwood-managed storage by default?

If you can reply with bullet answers, we can close this for the SIG pack. Also if you have a single CSV with CIDRs we can put that into our firewall allowlist.

Best,
Anne

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Cho <anne.cho@deltabank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Request: short control-plane segregation + egress narrative for SIG

Anne — quick answers below (bullet form) so you can drop into your SIG workbook: 

1) Static egress IPs for Redwood-managed control plane (Dedicated): yes, we publish region-scoped static IP blocks. Ephemeral NATs are not used in production control-plane egress unless a customer is on a transient or sandbox environment that explicitly opts out of static allocation. We will provide CIDR blocks as CSV (see attached egress_policy_matrix.xlsx, tab "CIDR").

2) Private deployments with Redwood-managed control plane + private peering: telemetry and updates can be constrained to the private interconnect (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute) provided the customer enables route-ads and BGP filters on their side; in that configuration, no control-plane egress leaves the private link to the public internet. We document the required BGP routes and prefix lists in the PDF appendix.

3) KV caches and backup: KV caches are ephemeral and pinned to data-plane nodes. For Private on-prem and Private with customer-managed control plane we do not back those caches up to Redwood-managed object storage by default. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed) we collect operational metrics but not model payloads; backup of cache state is an opt-in feature and would be described explicitly in the data processing addendum.

Next steps: I can export the CIDR CSV and a short IP allowlist text file and send it to procurement. Would you like the 30-minute walkthrough on Aug 22 or a recorded 15-minute split-screen walkthrough?

Cheers,
Soojin

Security Architect | Redwood Inference
